e-12933.problem: Given that $P(A)=\dfrac12,$ $P(A \cap B)=\dfrac16,$ and $P(A \cup B)=\dfrac23,$ find $P(A'\cup B').$
e-12933.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $P(B)$ using the addition law:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A\cup B) & =P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B) \\ \frac{2}{3} & =\frac{1}{2}+P(B)-\frac{1}{6} \\ P(B) & =\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{6}-\frac{1}{2} \\ P(B) & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we construct the corresponding Venn diagram and shade the region $A'\cup B'.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14041480/assets/9856c9b0fdf3bf4b8f84417f6e625d823590f57dac4dcc8185994aef3f8c5e50.png)

Finally, we have

$$
P(A'\cup B') = \dfrac1{3} + \dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac56.
$$

content.problem: Given that $P(B)=\frac{11}{20},$ $P(A\cap B)=\frac{1}{4},$ and $P(A\cup B)=\frac{3}{4},$ find $P({A}^{′}\cap B).$
content.worked_solution:
First, we calculate $P(A)$ using the addition law:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A\cup B) & =P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B) \\ \frac{3}{4} & =P(A)+\frac{11}{20}-\frac{1}{4} \\ P(A) & =\frac{3}{4}-\frac{11}{20}+\frac{1}{4} \\ P(A) & =\frac{15}{20}-\frac{11}{20}+\frac{5}{20} \\ P(A) & =\frac{9}{20}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we construct the corresponding Venn diagram and shade the region ${A}^{′}\cap B.$

$$
P({A}^{′}\cap B)=\frac{3}{10}.
